title: Billionaire dataset — data ingestion + review operator spec
purpose: Raw research files land in the collection from external model runs, mining batches and user downloads, in WHATEVER shape the producer felt like. This job turns each drop into normalized dataset rows without corrupting what already exists. The importer is deliberately dumb: scripts/ingest.py reads a fixed list of expected files. The OPERATOR (you, the LLM) is the adaptive layer — you inspect each drop, conform it to a schema the pipeline already understands, record the classification judgment explicitly, and prove nothing was lost.

vars.PILE: /home/bobbigmac/projects/toys/open-source-research/billionaires — the raw collection; everything derives from here
vars.MASTER: {PILE}/pair_mining_master_2026-11-18/ — the master pack: current cumulative ledger + batch increments + registries + landed drops
vars.INGEST: scripts/ingest.py — rebuilds data/*.jsonl wholesale from {PILE}; BB_SRC env var overrides the pile root
vars.LEDGER: billionaire_pair_links_append_only_vN.csv — the cumulative pair-edge ledger; N increments on each new master
vars.OUT: data/*.jsonl — the normalized tables the microsite renders

invariants: NEVER edit or delete rows inside a cumulative ledger or an append-only file — new truth arrives as new rows/files; superseded versions stay on disk
NEVER mutate a downloaded drop — conform into a NEW file next to it; the original stays as-received
The join key is the person slug (Profile URI). Every a/b on an imported edge must resolve in people.jsonl — a typo or non-roster person is found BEFORE rebuild, not after

Every source_id referenced by an edge must resolve in sources.jsonl — a batch that mints its own id namespace (OLDREPORT/WEB-*, ISO*) ships or gets a registry CSV in the registry schema (source_id,title,url,source_type,coverage_note,accessed_date)

Classification is a per-batch JUDGMENT recorded in CURATED_LEDGER_BATCHES, never a heuristic — read the batch's actual rows (evidence_status, real URLs, caveats, what the relationship claims) before deciding curated_research vs api_related

The tier model is the product: curated_research renders 'Sourced', api_related renders 'Feed-labeled (Forbes /related feed, unverified)'. Misclassifying hand-sourced edges as api_related publishes a false provenance claim — the worst failure this job has
Rebuild is wholesale — a bad change corrupts ALL tables, not just the new rows. Diff row counts AND spot-check old records, not only new ones
Count-in == count-out, accounted: every incoming row ends as imported / merged-into-existing / rejected-with-reason. Report the arithmetic

contract.objective: Each pass: new files land in {MASTER}, ingest.py is pointed at them deliberately, data/*.jsonl is rebuilt, and the result is verified — with a written record of what each file was and what was done to it
contract.shape: Input shape is NEVER guaranteed. Ledger rows, reduced merge-contract CSVs (person_a_uri,person_b_uri,type,label,confidence,summary,urls), zips, READMEs, briefs. Assume nothing; inspect everything
contract.done: Done means: files landed in {MASTER} (raw + conformed), ingest.py wired, rebuild ran clean, verification checks all pass, docs/counts updated, and a report of what was imported/merged/rejected is given to the user

survey.about: find what arrived that isn't in the collection yet — usually ~/Downloads but ask if unsure

steps.name: list-candidates
steps.cmd: ls -lat ~/Downloads | head -40 — take anything plausibly dataset-related from the recent window; unrelated topics (other projects' ChatGPT dumps) stay out
steps.why: the user drops files continuously; filename patterns (billionaire_*, verified_*, brief-*, *.zip) are a hint, not a rule

steps.name: identify
steps.cmd: for zips: unzip -l into /tmp and extract there first; for CSVs: head -3 + wc -l; for md: head -40
steps.why: you cannot decide anything about a file you haven't opened

steps.name: dup-check
steps.cmd: md5sum candidates vs same-named files already in {PILE} — browser re-downloads (' (1).csv') are common
steps.why: identical bytes = already landed; different bytes = a new version to diff

inspect.about: figure out what each file actually IS before touching the pipeline — this is the step that can never be skipped or automated

steps.name: shape
steps.cmd: csv.DictReader: column list, row count, distinct batch_id/scope/status/evidence_status values, edge_id namespaces
steps.why: the same conceptual file arrives with different columns every time (full ledger schema vs 7-column merge contract vs something new)

steps.name: diff-vs-existing
steps.cmd: new ledger? diff its edge_ids against the currently-wired ledger — the delta IS the batch. pair rows? check which (a,b) pairs already exist in relationships.jsonl
steps.why: a vN+1 ledger is expected to be a superset — if rows are missing vs vN, say so loudly rather than assuming

steps.name: resolve-references
steps.cmd: every person slug -> people.jsonl; every source_id namespace -> sources.jsonl; every novel namespace needs a registry plan
steps.why: ghost people and dangling source ids are silent corruption — they only surface as missing labels in the UI

steps.name: quality-scan
steps.cmd: look for: BOM, ';' vs ' ; ' separators, float-formatted years ('1981.0'), blank required fields, edge_ids duplicated INSIDE the drop, ids with whitespace, urls that are feed URLs vs real articles
steps.why: poor quality is expected — these defects are normal, catch them here not in the output

decide.about: the per-batch classification judgment — the decision the pipeline refuses to make for you

steps.name: classify-batch
steps.cmd: read the batch's rows: hand-sourced edges with named external sources + evidence summaries + interpretation caveats => curated_research (add batch_id to CURATED_LEDGER_BATCHES in ingest.py). Feed/discovery signals (profile /related labels, cohort projections, unverified assertions) => api_related default. Shared-asset/holding projections => derived_*
steps.why: this is a provenance decision that publishes as the Sourced/Feed-labeled tier — when unsure, read more rows; if still unsure, ask the user rather than guessing

conform.about: transform the drop into a schema an existing reader understands — YOU adapt the data, the parser does not adapt to the data

steps.name: conform-to-contract
steps.cmd: write a NEW csv in {MASTER} with the full ledger column set (edge_id,batch_id,person_a_uri,person_a_name,person_b_uri,person_b_name,relationship_type,relationship_label,scope,confidence,evidence_status,status,time_start,time_end,evidence_summary,interpretation_caveat,source_ids,source_urls,appended_on). Mint edge_ids in a batch-namespaced pattern (VRT-0001…). Resolve person names from people.jsonl. Fill provenance fields (batch_id, evidence_status, appended_on) honestly; leave genuinely unknown fields empty rather than fabricating
steps.why: worked example: verified_roster_ties.csv (7 cols) -> billionaire_verified_ties_2026-11-19_append_edges.csv (19 cols). The raw drop stays beside it for audit

steps.name: register-sources
steps.cmd: if the drop references source ids with no registry entries, write {MASTER}/billionaire_<batch>_sources_<date>.csv in registry schema; where id->url mapping is ambiguous (N ids vs M urls), map by best positional judgment and note that edges carry verbatim source_urls anyway

wire.about: point the dumb importer at the conformed files — every change is explicit and reviewable

steps.name: ledger-list
steps.cmd: update the ledger list in build_relationships() to the NEWEST cumulative ledger filename; add conformed edge files to the same loop
steps.why: versioned filenames never auto-pick — the newest is whichever actually landed (v6 -> v7 -> v8 so far)

steps.name: batch-registry
steps.cmd: add curated batch_ids to CURATED_LEDGER_BATCHES; add new source-registry files to the list in build_sources()
steps.why: these two lists ARE the recorded per-batch judgment

rebuild.about: regenerate the tables and prove the result

steps.name: run-ingest
steps.why: wholesale rebuild — every table is rewritten from the pile

steps.name: verify
steps.cmd: checks below — all must pass before reporting done

document.about: leave the trail a future pass needs

steps.name: update-counts
steps.cmd: data/README.md table row counts + the 'people have a curated tie' figure; {MASTER}/billionaire_pair_mining_master_README.md file list
steps.why: docs rot the moment a batch lands

steps.name: report
steps.cmd: tell the user: files landed, what each was, imported/merged/rejected arithmetic, classification calls made, anything skipped and why
steps.why: the review half of the job — the user sanity-checks your judgment calls

checks.row-arithmetic: new relationships == incoming rows - merges - explained rejections; print it, don't estimate it
checks.dangling-source-ids: every source_id on relationships+memberships resolves in sources.jsonl — must be zero
checks.ghost-people: every a/b resolves in people.jsonl — must be zero (checked pre-rebuild at inspect, re-checked after)
checks.new-edge-spot-check: read 2-3 new records in relationships.jsonl: expected origin, class, real source_urls, caveat_id present where the batch had caveats
checks.old-data-intact: counts of pre-existing batches/origins unchanged vs the pre-rebuild manifest; spot-check an old curated edge survives untouched
checks.render-check: node build.js --out /tmp/bb_preview — new edges appear at the expected tier; no console errors

failure-modes.mode: assuming last drop's schema — columns, separators and id conventions change every single time
failure-modes.check: inspect phase exists precisely because of this; never wire a file you haven't DictReader'd

failure-modes.mode: ledger version drift — vN+1 lands but ingest still reads vN, new edges silently absent
failure-modes.check: the ledger list always names the newest landed version; diff edge_ids old-vs-new first

failure-modes.mode: hand-sourced batch defaults to api_related -> published as 'Forbes feed, unverified' — false provenance at the Sourced/Feed tier boundary
failure-modes.check: CURATED_LEDGER_BATCHES review each pass; new-edge spot-check reads the origin field

failure-modes.mode: edge_id collision across drops — first-writer-wins dedupe silently discards the later rows
failure-modes.check: mint batch-namespaced ids when conforming; check incoming ids against existing ones at inspect

failure-modes.mode: same pair at a stronger tier treated as a duplicate and dropped — dedupe key is (pair|origin|class), so a curated upgrade is a NEW record and MUST land
failure-modes.check: 18 of the first VRT drop's pairs already existed at weaker tiers; all 51 still imported

failure-modes.mode: dangling source ids when a batch mints its own namespace
failure-modes.check: dangling-source-ids check == zero; registry CSV written per new namespace

failure-modes.mode: non-pair data (external context leads, entity files, briefs) force-fit into the pair pipeline — they belong to different tables or are research queue, not edges
failure-modes.check: classify the ARTIFACT, not just the batch: leads/briefs land in {MASTER} for provenance without necessarily becoming rows

failure-modes.mode: wholesale rebuild corrupts pre-existing tables via an unrelated ingest edit
failure-modes.check: old-data-intact check: pre-existing batch counts identical pre/post rebuild
